monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity and efficiency this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — evidenced by faster paces, higher HR, more Z3–Z4 time, and improved aerobic efficiency and cadence.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved from 13.42 to 13.8 — the largest single-month gain in your log — reflecting better running economy despite higher average HR and faster paces.

goal_tracker.message: You need 8.3 more km across 3 sessions in the remaining 14 days to match last month’s volume — e.g., three 3-km runs (9.0 km total) at Zone 2 HR ≤138 bpm would exceed the target while supporting recovery and consistency.

insights.title: Efficiency up despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.8 even as avg HR increased +7 bpm and avg pace improved by 36 sec/km — indicating meaningful neuromuscular and metabolic adaptation to mixed-intensity work.

insights.title: Shift toward threshold and tempo effort
insights.body: Z3–Z4 time jumped from 22% (19% Z3 + 3% Z4) in May to 43% (27% Z3 + 16% Z4) in June — a strategic intensification, but Z1 dropped sharply from 36% to 20%, risking under-recovery if sustained.

insights.title: Cadence and ground contact time diverging
insights.body: Cadence improved (+6 spm), yet ground contact time remained stable (~313 ms avg) and vertical oscillation stayed low (7.6–9.2 cm), suggesting form gains are driven by turnover rather than reduced braking — consistent with recent faster efforts like the 6:33 min/km (392 sec/km) run.

insights.title: High-intensity density without Z5 progression
insights.body: Z5 remains minimal (2% this month, 0% last month), yet Z4 increased 13 percentage points — indicating growing tolerance for near-threshold work, but no true VO2 max stimulus has been added, limiting ceiling development.

recommendations.action: Do one 5-km Zone 2 run at avg HR ≤138 bpm before June 23rd, using your May 2026 avg HR of 136 bpm as a ceiling reference.
recommendations.reason: Your Z1 time dropped to 20% and avg HR rose +7 bpm; reintroducing a dedicated low-HR session will support autonomic recovery and sustain aerobic base gains.

recommendations.action: Add one 6-min Z4 interval (e.g., 4 x 90-sec @ Z4, 90-sec jog recovery) on a non-long-run day, targeting avg HR 155–162 bpm based on your recent 6:33/km effort (HR 159).
recommendations.reason: Z4 volume increased significantly (16% vs 3%), but structured intervals will improve lactate buffering and ensure quality — especially given your best pace (392 sec/km) occurred at 159 bpm.

recommendations.action: Perform a 10-min post-run mobility routine focusing on hip flexors and calves after your next run, referencing your elevated ground contact time (311–317 ms) and stride length stability (~69–70 cm on long runs).
recommendations.reason: Stable GCT and low stride length on long runs suggest emerging fatigue or stiffness; targeted mobility can preserve efficiency as weekly intensity rises.

weekly_focus.description: This week prioritizes sustaining your newfound efficiency and pace gains while preventing overreliance on mid-to-high zones — using one low-HR run, one structured Z4 session, and daily movement hygiene to protect form and readiness.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (5 km, HR ≤138 bpm)
Z4 interval session (4 x 90-sec @ Z4, 90-sec jog)
Recovery-focused easy run (3–4 km, HR ≤132 bpm, cadence ≥150 spm)
